title: The mina, and what a back carries
text:
A **mina** is fifty shekels: about half a kilogram of silver, near enough to a bag of sugar held in one hand. Sixty minas make a **talent**, some twenty-eight kilograms — a load for two people and a carrying pole, not for one.

Goods are weighed in the same minas. A copper ingot is four minas, about two kilograms; a jar of oil is three; a porter's full load is twenty, about nine kilos. A traveler on foot carries no more than a porter does.

Those numbers are how the goods in this market are counted against one another. They are not a record of what any yard charged.

sources: Syrian weight system: 50 shekels to the mina, 60 minas to the talent, general
Ras Shamra economic tablets on weighed commodities, general
provenance.notes: The mina and talent ratios are attested for the Syrian system, and a mina of the order of 470 g. The exact standard varied by city and period (plausible for Ugarit). The weights of goods in play are game figures, not a metrological table; the kilogram gloss is the reader's.
